items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: Now the other trumpet players, like Freddie Hubbard and Lee Morgan and Clifford Brown, they all had great sounds but they were very big and more brassy kind of sound.

ctx.x: Yes, I say sorta kinda. I went through grammar school and high school and I was a little bit of a maverick you might say, a bit of a nonconformist in a way. My father had always taught me to follow my own voice, myself. That is a very, very strong concept that I think has always pervaded throughout this music. You know, particularly in the history of it. That the individual, the individuality and the originality is very important I think to the character of jazz. And so my father had always encouraged me to do…
